data.title: bn-i3ak: Prove typed MySQL sessions across SingleStore and MySQL 8
data.description: Review the portable pinned live-acceptance harness, hostile protocol peers, real Sigil component/Lua evidence, teardown, docs, and 256-case session state-machine property coverage. Exact base e9659bb2; no production component bytes changed.

data.body: HIGH: Teardown leaks the MySQL image anonymous /var/lib/mysql volume. The script calls container rm without --volumes, then checks only remaining containers. I reproduced this with the exact pinned image: podman create attached anonymous volume 58828e0b..., and podman rm left it present. Docker has the same rm -v requirement. Each live run can retain database state and consume storage, while README claims no durable volume and teardown.txt reports success. Remove anonymous volumes during teardown and verify their exact IDs are absent before writing the success marker.

HIGH: The packaged-path fault matrix does not prove numeric overflow. The bone explicitly requires overflow classification independently of implementation unit fixtures. This peer sends malformed metadata, nonnumeric text, and an oversized packet, but never a signed or unsigned value outside the declared MySQL integer range. The base protocol unit tests cover overflow, yet this live acceptance cannot detect a broken component binding or packaged execution path for that case. Add an overflow statement and require its encoding failure, terminal EOF, exact trace, and no reconnect/replay.

data.reason: Two HIGH acceptance blockers: the portable teardown leaks the pinned MySQL image anonymous data volume, and the packaged-path hostile peer omits the required numeric-overflow case. See th-nowsa0 and th-igrfx5.

Fixed in d03b2989: inventory exact managed container and volume IDs before cleanup, remove containers with portable --volumes, explicitly remove newly created residual volumes, verify every container/volume absent, and record global volume inventories before/after. Final live evidence run.Wd0Tkypv shows the MySQL volume present before cleanup, absent after, and no global volume delta.

Fixed in d03b2989: packaged component/Lua hostile path now sends signed TINYINT 128, asserts exact terminal protocol class/no partial result/post-error closed, records the statement exactly once on one connection, requires EOF, and rejects a fifth connection. Final live evidence run.Wd0Tkypv records 4 exact queries/connections and 4 terminal EOFs.

data.body: HIGH: SIGINT and SIGTERM can make an interrupted acceptance run exit 0. Bash enters a signal trap with the prior command status, not a forced signal status. cleanup captures that value and exits it. Because the same function is also the EXIT trap, the signal path runs cleanup twice. I reproduced the exact trap pattern: kill -TERM $$ after a successful command produced cleanup-status=0 twice and process rc=0. This is a false-green acceptance gate despite safe resource removal. Use dedicated INT/TERM handlers that invoke one idempotent cleanup with nonzero signal status, and disable traps before exit. Add a deterministic signal-path regression that proves nonzero exit plus container and volume absence.

data.reason: The two prior blockers are fixed and live acceptance is green, but the INT/TERM trap can exit zero and run cleanup twice. See new HIGH thread.

data.body: Verified at d03b2989: the harness inventories attached volumes, uses rm --volumes, removes only newly created fallback volumes, and proves exact managed absence. Live run Z7RnKKMH captured MySQL volume 17d8cbf4... present before cleanup and absent after. External engine volume count 159 and sorted inventory hash dbe481fe... were identical before and after.

Verified at d03b2989: the packaged component/Lua path sends signed TINYINT value 128, returns protocol with no rows, latches closed, and closes the peer connection. Live evidence records four exact queries, four terminal EOFs, and no fifth connection.

data.reason: Fixed in 2d53e9c: shared dispatcher passes explicit 130/143 for INT/TERM, preserves ordinary EXIT status, disables EXIT and ignores further signals before cleanup, and guards cleanup once. Deterministic check runs TERM, INT, and EXIT in isolated subprocesses, asserts exact rc, one cleanup-count line, and both managed-resource sentinels absent. Final live run xfZLUClV has one cleanup-count line (0), exact container/volume absence, and unchanged global volume inventory.

data.body: Verified at 2d53e9ca. The dispatcher clears EXIT, ignores INT/TERM during cleanup, guards reentry, and exits the callback status. The isolated regression proves INT=130, TERM=143, ordinary EXIT=37, one callback, and resource absence. Full live run SPbLMoLt recorded one cleanup line with status 0 and removed both containers plus exact volume fceaca57... .

data.reason: LGTM exact 2d53e9cafe5a496eeb41c1fd3289111392a980f6. Signal cleanup, volume cleanup, overflow path, full pinned live matrix, static gates, and exact artifact digests verified.
